Find the polar coordinates of the intersection points of the polar curves  $r=2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ and $r=1,$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
To determine the polar coordinates of the intersection points, we will solve the following system of equations for $r$ and $\theta :$  

$$
\begin{aligned}\,r & =2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \,r & =1\end{aligned}
$$

We begin by setting the equations equal to each other and solve for $\theta .$ This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation in the interval $[{0}^{∘},{360}^{∘}),$ we obtain ${\theta }_{1}={30}^{∘}$ and ${\theta }_{2}={150}^{∘}.$  

Notice that we must have $r=1$ for any point that lies on both curves. 

Therefore, the polar coordinates of the points of intersection are

$\,$ $(r,\theta )=(1,{30}^{∘})\,$ and $\,(r,\theta )=(1,{150}^{∘}).$
